+    uv run uvicorn api.server:app --port 8000
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import asyncio
+import json
+import logging
+import time
+from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
+from pathlib import Path
+from typing import Any
+
+from fastapi import FastAPI, HTTPException
+from fastapi.middleware.cors import CORSMiddleware
+from fastapi.responses import StreamingResponse
+from pydantic import BaseModel
+
+from api.runtime import Runtime
+from harbor import deploy as deploys
+from harbor import releases
+from harbor.agent import effective_config
+from nightshift import actions as ns_actions
+from nightshift import detector, policy, provenance, reporter
+from nightshift.runner import approve
+from ops import clock
+from ops.db import loads
+from ops.economics import load_economics
+from ops.settings import REPO_DIR, settings
+
+logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(asctime)s %(levelname)s %(name)s: %(message)s")
+runtime: Runtime | None = None
+
+
+@asynccontextmanager
+async def lifespan(_: FastAPI):
+    global runtime
+    runtime = Runtime()
+    runtime.bus.bind(asyncio.get_running_loop())
+    runtime.start()
+    yield
+    runtime.stop()
+
+
+app = FastAPI(title="Night Shift", lifespan=lifespan)
+app.add_middleware(CORSMiddleware, allow_origins=["*"], allow_methods=["*"], allow_headers=["*"])
+
+
+def rt() -> Runtime:
+    assert runtime is not None
+    return runtime
+
+
+def _incident_row(r: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    return {
+        "id": r["id"], "status": r["status"], "type": r["type"], "severity": r["severity"], "title": r["title"],
+        "summary": r["summary"], "opened_at": r["opened_at"], "mitigated_at": r["mitigated_at"],
+        "resolved_at": r["resolved_at"], "impact": loads(r["impact_json"], None),
+    }
+
+
+# -- reads ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+@app.get("/api/health")
+def health() -> dict[str, Any]:
+    return {"ok": True, "brain": rt().brain, "llm": settings.llm_available, "neatlogs": settings.neatlogs_available}
+
+
+@app.get("/api/state")
+def state() -> dict[str, Any]:
+    r = rt()
+    cfg = effective_config(r.db)
+    stats, base, signals = detector.detect(r.db, since=r.nightshift.quiet_since())
+    open_inc = r.nightshift.open_incident()
+    totals = r.db.one("SELECT COUNT(*) n, COALESCE(SUM(loss_usd),0) loss, COALESCE(SUM(cost_usd),0) cost "
+                      "FROM conversations WHERE replay = 0") or {}
+    now = clock.local_now()
+    return {
+        "brain": r.brain,
+        "local_time": now.strftime("%H:%M:%S"),
+        "local_time_simulated": clock.is_simulated(),
+        "release": cfg.release.id, "release_title": cfg.release.title, "model": cfg.model,
+        "flags": cfg.flags, "max_steps": cfg.max_steps, "outage_models": sorted(cfg.outage_models),
+        "control": r.db.control_snapshot(),
+        "traffic": {"running": r.traffic.running, "per_minute": r.traffic.per_minute,
+                    "attack_share": r.traffic.mix.attack_share},
+        "nightshift_enabled": r.nightshift.enabled,
+        "window": stats.as_dict(), "baseline": base, "signals": [s.__dict__ for s in signals],
+        "open_incident": _incident_row(open_inc) if open_inc else None,
+        "totals": totals,
+        "budget": r.budget(),
+        "economics": {"conversations_per_minute": load_economics().conversations_per_minute(now),
+                      "human_response_minutes": load_economics().human_response_minutes(now)},
+    }
+
+
+@app.get("/api/metrics")
+def metrics(minutes: int = 15, bucket_s: int = 30) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    since = time.time() - minutes * 60
+    rows = rt().db.query("SELECT ts, outcome, loss_usd, cost_usd, steps, release, model FROM conversations "
+                         "WHERE replay = 0 AND ts >= ? ORDER BY ts", [since])
+    buckets: dict[int, dict[str, Any]] = {}
+    for row in rows:
+        b = int(row["ts"] // bucket_s * bucket_s)
+        d = buckets.setdefault(b, {"t": b, "n": 0, "loss": 0.0, "cost": 0.0, "failed": 0, "wrong_refund": 0,
+                                   "escalated": 0, "correct": 0, "steps": 0})
+        d["n"] += 1
+        d["loss"] += row["loss_usd"] or 0
+        d["cost"] += row["cost_usd"] or 0
+        d["steps"] += row["steps"] or 0
+        if row["outcome"] in ("failed", "wrong_refund", "escalated", "correct"):
+            d[row["outcome"]] += 1

+

+
+@app.get("/api/benchmark")
+def benchmark() -> dict[str, Any]:
+    root = REPO_DIR / "evidence" / "benchmark"
+    runs = sorted([p for p in root.glob("*-live") if (p / "results.json").exists()], reverse=True) if root.exists() else []
+    if not runs:
+        runs = sorted([p for p in root.glob("*") if (p / "results.json").exists()], reverse=True) if root.exists() else []
+    if not runs:
+        return {"run": None, "results": []}
+    run: Path = runs[0]
+    return {"run": run.name, "results": json.loads((run / "results.json").read_text())}
+
+
+@app.get("/api/economics")
+def economics() -> dict[str, Any]:
+    e = load_economics()
+    return {"unit_economics": e.raw, "churn_cost": e.churn_cost, "policy": policy.load_policy()}
+
+
+# -- demo controls ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+class DeployIn(BaseModel):
+    release: str
+    actor: str = "developer"
+
+
+class FaultIn(BaseModel):
+    kind: str = "provider_outage"
+    value: str | None = "claude-haiku"
+
+
+class AttackIn(BaseModel):
+    share: float = 0.5
+
+
+class TrafficIn(BaseModel):
+    running: bool = True
+    per_minute: float | None = None
+
+
+class ToggleIn(BaseModel):
+    enabled: bool
+
+
+@app.post("/api/demo/reset")
+def demo_reset() -> dict[str, Any]:
+    rt().reset()
+    return {"ok": True}
+
+
+@app.post("/api/demo/deploy")
+def demo_deploy(body: DeployIn) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    try:
+        return rt().deploy(body.release, body.actor)
+    except FileNotFoundError as exc:
+        raise HTTPException(404, str(exc)) from exc
+
+
+@app.post("/api/demo/fault")
+def demo_fault(body: FaultIn) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    rt().set_fault(body.kind, body.value)
+    return {"ok": True, "control": rt().db.control_snapshot()}
+
+
+@app.post("/api/demo/attack")
+def demo_attack(body: AttackIn) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    rt().set_attack(body.share)
+    return {"ok": True}
+
+
+@app.post("/api/traffic")
+def traffic(body: TrafficIn) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    rt().set_traffic(body.running, body.per_minute)
+    return {"running": rt().traffic.running, "per_minute": rt().traffic.per_minute}
+
+
+@app.post("/api/nightshift")
+def toggle_nightshift(body: ToggleIn) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    rt().nightshift.enabled = body.enabled
+    rt().bus.publish({"type": "nightshift", "enabled": body.enabled})
+    return {"enabled": body.enabled}
+
+
+@app.post("/api/actions/{action_id}/approve")
+def approve_action(action_id: int) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    res = approve(rt().db, action_id, actor="console")
+    rt().bus.publish({"type": "action", "action_id": action_id, "result": res})
+    return res
+
+
+@app.post("/api/actions/{action_id}/undo")
+def undo_action(action_id: int) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    note = ns_actions.undo(rt().db, action_id)
+    rt().bus.publish({"type": "action", "action_id": action_id, "result": note})
+    return {"result": note}
+
+
+@app.get("/api/stream")
+async def stream() -> StreamingResponse:
+    bus = rt().bus
+    q = bus.subscribe()
+
+    async def gen():
+        try:
+            yield "retry: 2000\n\n"
+            while True:
+                try:
+                    event = await asyncio.wait_for(q.get(), timeout=15)
+                    yield f"data: {json.dumps(event, default=str)}\n\n"
+                except asyncio.TimeoutError:
+                    yield ": keep-alive\n\n"
+        finally:
+            bus.unsubscribe(q)
+
+    return StreamingResponse(gen(), media_type="text/event-stream",
+                             headers={"Cache-Control": "no-cache", "X-Accel-Buffering": "no"})

Snapshot-Restore Scheduling for Persistent Agent Micro-VMs
Ary Shrivastava, Maria Gorskikh, and Brandon Li
September 3, 2026
Abstract

Long-lived software agents spend most of their lifetime idle, yet the conventional deployment keeps a full virtual machine resident for each of them. We study a scheduler that snapshots an idle guest to disk and restores it on the next inbound message, so that a parked agent costs only its storage. We characterise the restore path, show that its latency is dominated by page-cache warm-up rather than by the hypervisor, and give a bound on the expected monthly cost of an agent as a function of its wake rate.

1  Introduction

A persistent agent is a process with a disk, a set of credentials, and a schedule of its own. Unlike a request handler, it has state that outlives any single interaction, which rules out the stateless scaling model of serverless platforms. We model an agent as an alternating sequence of awake and asleep intervals and write a(t) ∈ {0, 1} for its state at time t. The cost over a horizon T is then

C(T) = csST + cv ∫0T a(t) dt
(1)

story="'Honor finance pre-approved refunds' meets attackers who write the approval themselves."),
+# INC-1010-01-89de: r42 system prompt stripped policy guardrails, causing mass unnecessary escalations

+Release r42 (commit 48838b2bcdcd, deployed ~0.2 min before onset) rewrote the system prompt to 3 lines for brevity, silently dropping all policy enforcement rules from r41: (1) the mandatory `check_refund_policy` call before any refund, (2) the instruction to follow its decision exactly and never exceed `max_refund`, (3) the rule to explain ineligibility and NOT refund/escalate when `eligible=false` and `requires_human=false`. The new prompt says "resolve refund requests in one step: look up the order and refund it." When the agent calls `check_refund_policy` and gets `eligible=false, requires_human=false`, it has no instruction to deny the request — so it defaults to escalating to a human instead of closing the ticket with a policy explanation. This caused 40% escalation rate (baseline 17%). All 4 sampled failing conversations show the same pattern: policy returns ineligible/not-requires-human, agent escalates anyway, graded as "escalated a request policy could settle."
+- Commit: `48838b2bcdcd` Release r42: shorter, friendlier replies

+- Prompt behind the change: “Customers say Harbor's support replies are too long and robotic. Create a new release file backend/harbor/releases/r42.yaml, based on backend/harbor/releases/r41.yaml (same fields, id r42, title 'Shorter, friendlier replies'). Rewrite the system prompt to be about three short lines: who Harbor is, keep replies brief and warm, and resolve refund requests in one step (look up the order and refund it”
+- Loss rate at detection: **$7.12/min** at production volume (7.0 conversations/min)
+- Human response time at 03:17 local: 300.0 min → projected loss if waiting: **$2,137**
+- Unit economics: cfo.ai model 'Harbor Goods — support economics' (mirror; pending sync)

+- [needs_approval] `deploy_code_fix` {"summary": "When rewriting the system prompt for tone/brevity, preserve all policy-enforcement rules as a separate, non-negotiable section. Add a CI/CD prompt-regression test that asserts: for an ineligible order with requires_human=false, the agent must reply with a denial (not escalate). The coding agent itself flagged this risk in its note \u2014 a human review gate on system prompt changes should be required before merging.", "revert_commit": "48838b2bcdcdb937b0cafa77785fb595aa26ee9f", "release": "r42"} — proposed — forward fix: needs human approval
+- [auto] `rollback_release` {"target": "r41"} — applied — 'rollback_release' is pre-approved and reversible in one step; confidence 0.98 ≥ 0.6; projected loss while waiting for a human $2,137 ≥ $25
+- Live metrics after action: metrics back within baseline

+When rewriting the system prompt for tone/brevity, preserve all policy-enforcement rules as a separate, non-negotiable section. """Night Shift business model (draft mirrored into cfo.ai).

Computes a 24-month plan — pricing, unit costs, revenue, costs, cash and runway — from the
assumptions below and the investigation costs measured in the latest live benchmark.
Writes business/PLAN.md and web/public/business.json.

+def write(plan: dict) -> None:

"""Log in to the cfo.ai MCP server with the OAuth device flow (approve from any browser or phone).

    uv run python scripts/cfo_login.py          # prints a link + code, waits for approval
    uv run python scripts/cfo_login.py --check  # lists the cfo.ai MCP tools with the saved token

The token is saved to <repo>/.cfo_token.json (gitignored). Then, to let Claude Code build the
model in cfo.ai:

    claude mcp add --transport http cfoai https://api.cfo.ai/mcp \
        --header "Authorization: Bearer $(python -c 'import json;print(json.load(open(\"../.cfo_token.json\"))[\"access_token\"])')"
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

import httpx

AUTH = "https://complete-cottage-73.authkit.app"
MCP = "https://api.cfo.ai/mcp"
TOKEN_FILE = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / ".cfo_token.json"


def register() -> str:
    r = httpx.post(f"{AUTH}/oauth2/register", json={
        "client_name": "Night Shift",
        "grant_types": ["urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code", "refresh_token", "authorization_code"],
        "token_endpoint_auth_method": "none",
        "redirect_uris": ["http://localhost:8765/callback"],
        "response_types": ["code"],
    }, timeout=20)
    r.raise_for_status()
    return r.json()["client_id"]


def login() -> dict:
    client_id = register()
    d = httpx.post(f"{AUTH}/oauth2/device_authorization", data={
        "client_id": client_id, "scope": "openid profile email offline_access", "resource": MCP,
    }, timeout=20).json()
    print("\n  Approve Night Shift's access to cfo.ai:")
    print(f"  {d['verification_uri_complete']}")
    print(f"  code: {d['user_code']}   (expires in {d['expires_in'] // 60} min)\n", flush=True)
    deadline = time.time() + d["expires_in"]
    interval = d.get("interval", 5)
    while time.time() < deadline:
        time.sleep(interval)
        t = httpx.post(f"{AUTH}/oauth2/token", data={
            "grant_type": "urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code",
            "device_code": d["device_code"], "client_id": client_id,
        }, timeout=20)
        body = t.json()
        if t.status_code == 200 and "access_token" in body:
            body["client_id"] = client_id
            body["obtained_at"] = time.time()
            TOKEN_FILE.write_text(json.dumps(body))
            TOKEN_FILE.chmod(0o600)
            print(f"  ✓ logged in; token saved to {TOKEN_FILE.name}")
            return body
        if body.get("error") == "slow_down":
            interval += 5
        elif body.get("error") not in ("authorization_pending", None):
            sys.exit(f"login failed: {body}")
    sys.exit("login expired; run again")


def mcp_call(token: str, method: str, params: dict | None = None, session: str | None = None) -> tuple[dict, str | None]:
    headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}", "Content-Type": "application/json",
               "Accept": "application/json, text/event-stream"}
    if session:
        headers["Mcp-Session-Id"] = session
    r = httpx.post(MCP, headers=headers, json={"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "method": method, "params": params or {}},
                   timeout=60)
    sid = r.headers.get("mcp-session-id", session)
    text = r.text
    for line in text.splitlines():
        if line.startswith("data:"):
            return json.loads(line[5:]), sid
    return (json.loads(text) if text.strip() else {}), sid


def check() -> None:
    token = json.loads(TOKEN_FILE.read_text())["access_token"]
    init, sid = mcp_call(token, "initialize", {"protocolVersion": "2025-06-18", "capabilities": {},
                                               "clientInfo": {"name": "nightshift", "version": "0.1"}})
    print("server:", init.get("result", {}).get("serverInfo"))
    tools, _ = mcp_call(token, "tools/list", {}, sid)
    for t in tools.get("result", {}).get("tools", []):
        print(f"- {t['name']}: {t.get('description', '')[:110]}")
    orgs, _ = mcp_call(token, "tools/call", {"name": "list_orgs", "arguments": {}}, sid)
    print("orgs:", json.dumps(orgs.get("result", {}))[:600])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--check", action="store_true")
    args = ap.parse_args()
    if args.check:
        check()
    else:
        login()
        check()

"""Log in to the cfo.ai MCP server with the OAuth device flow (approve from any browser or phone).

    uv run python scripts/cfo_login.py          # prints a link + code, waits for approval
    uv run python scripts/cfo_login.py --check  # lists the cfo.ai MCP tools with the saved token

The token is saved to <repo>/.cfo_token.json (gitignored). Then, to let Claude Code build the
model in cfo.ai:

    claude mcp add --transport http cfoai https://api.cfo.ai/mcp \
        --header "Authorization: Bearer $(python -c 'import json;print(json.load(open(\"../.cfo_token.json\"))[\"access_token\"])')"
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

import httpx

AUTH = "https://complete-cottage-73.authkit.app"
MCP = "https://api.cfo.ai/mcp"
TOKEN_FILE = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / ".cfo_token.json"


def register() -> str:
    r = httpx.post(f"{AUTH}/oauth2/register", json={
        "client_name": "Night Shift",
        "grant_types": ["urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code", "refresh_token", "authorization_code"],
        "token_endpoint_auth_method": "none",
        "redirect_uris": ["http://localhost:8765/callback"],
        "response_types": ["code"],
    }, timeout=20)
    r.raise_for_status()
    return r.json()["client_id"]


def login() -> dict:
    client_id = register()
    d = httpx.post(f"{AUTH}/oauth2/device_authorization", data={
        "client_id": client_id, "scope": "openid profile email offline_access", "resource": MCP,
    }, timeout=20).json()
    print("\n  Approve Night Shift's access to cfo.ai:")
    print(f"  {d['verification_uri_complete']}")
    print(f"  code: {d['user_code']}   (expires in {d['expires_in'] // 60} min)\n", flush=True)
    deadline = time.time() + d["expires_in"]
    interval = d.get("interval", 5)
    while time.time() < deadline:
        time.sleep(interval)
        t = httpx.post(f"{AUTH}/oauth2/token", data={
            "grant_type": "urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code",
            "device_code": d["device_code"], "client_id": client_id,
        }, timeout=20)
        body = t.json()
        if t.status_code == 200 and "access_token" in body:
            body["client_id"] = client_id
            body["obtained_at"] = time.time()

    headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}", "Content-Type": "application/json",
               "Accept": "application/json, text/event-stream"}

        headers["Mcp-Session-Id"] = session

    text = r.text
    for line in text.splitlines():

    return (json.loads(text) if text.strip() else {}), sid

    orgs, _ = mcp_call(token, "tools/call", {"name": "list_orgs", "arguments": {}}, sid)
    print("orgs:", json.dumps(orgs.get("result", {}))[:600])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--check", action="store_true")
    args = ap.parse_args()
    if args.check:
        check()
    else:
        login()
        check()

# Building the plan in cfo.ai

Two models live in cfo.ai. Night Shift reads the first one at runtime (mirrored into
`business/unit_economics.yaml`); the second is the plan we submit.

## 1. Harbor Goods — support economics (what an incident costs)

Prompt for Ari (or for Claude Code with the cfo.ai MCP attached):

> Build a model called "Harbor Goods — support economics" for an online outdoor-gear store whose
> customer support is handled by an AI agent. Variables: support conversations per hour (day 480,
> night 90), customer lifetime value $260, probability a customer churns after a failed support
> conversation 8%, fully loaded cost of a human support ticket $4.50, chargeback fee $15, dispute rate
> on wrongly denied refunds 25%. Derive: cost of a failed conversation (churn × LTV = $20.80), cost of
> a missed refund, and cost per minute of an incident given a loss-per-conversation input. Add an
> on-call table: minutes until a human responds (business hours 15, evening 45, night 300). Add a
> scenario "Night incident" with loss per conversation $50 at night volume and show the projected
> loss if nobody acts until morning.

## 2. Night Shift — business plan (pricing, costs, revenue, runway)

> Build a 24-month plan for "Night Shift", a SaaS that acts as the on-call engineer for companies running
> customer-facing AI agents. Use the assumptions and measured unit costs in the table below (from
> business/PLAN.md, generated by business/model.py from our live benchmark). Pricing: Hobby $0, Team
> $399/month, Scale $1,990/month, 15% of paying customers on Scale. Costs: 2 founders at $4,500/month,
> first engineer from month 9 at $5,500/month, base infrastructure $400/month, $18 per customer per
> month infrastructure, LLM cost per customer from measured investigations, 3.5% payment fees,
> marketing $1,500/month from month 4. Starting cash $150,000. New paid customers ramp 0,0,1,2,3…
> to 22 per month, 3% monthly logo churn. Show MRR, costs, net burn, cash, runway and break-even month.
> Add scenarios: "Slow sales" (half the new customers) and "LLM prices double".

Then share each model as a read-only Page and put the link in `web/public/business.json`
(`cfo_share_url`) and in the README, and export the plan into `business/`.

# Demo script — 3:00 max

Setup (before recording):
```bash
cd backend && NIGHTSHIFT_LOCAL_TIME=03:07 uv run uvicorn api.server:app --port 8000   # live models
cd web && npm run dev                                                                # http://localhost:3000
```
In the console: Reset demo → Start traffic (12/min). Let ~10 conversations go green. Have the
phone (ntfy app subscribed to `NTFY_TOPIC`) on camera if possible; otherwise the on-screen phone.

| Time | Screen | Say |
|---|---|---|
| 0:00–0:15 | Landing hero | "It's 3:07 AM. Your support agent is talking to customers. Nobody is awake. Night Shift is the on-call engineer for AI agents: it stops the bleeding by itself and only wakes you for decisions that can't be undone." |
| 0:15–0:35 | Console, quiet | "This is Harbor, a real LLM support agent on Claude Haiku, handling refunds for a store. Every conversation is traced in **neatlogs**. Every release was written by a Claude Code session and checkpointed by **Entire**." |
| 0:35–0:50 | Click "r46 One-step refunds" | "A developer asked their coding agent to make refunds faster — and assumed the payments service validates eligibility. It doesn't." Money counter turns red. |
| 0:50–1:35 | Incident panel streams | "Night Shift detects wrong refunds from the ledger, then investigates like an SRE: reads the traces from neatlogs, sees the deploy, diffs the release, and follows the commit to the **Entire checkpoint** — here's the exact prompt behind the bug, and the warning the coding agent gave that nobody read." |

# #neatHack build-in-public drafts

Drafts only — Aman reviews, edits and posts. Replace bracketed bits with real links.

## 1 — the idea
Building Night Shift for #neatHack: the on-call engineer for AI agents.

At 3 AM a "harmless" prompt change starts paying refunds it shouldn't. Every request still returns 200.
Night Shift catches it, finds the change *and the coding-agent prompt behind it*, prices the damage,
rolls back within a pre-approved policy, proves the fix, and only then pages you.

Stack: @neatlogs traces · Entire checkpoints · cfo.ai economics. [repo link]

## 2 — the bad releases are real
Every bad release in our benchmark was written by a real Claude Code session with a realistic dev
request — "make refunds one step, payments already validates them". Entire checkpointed each one.

Best part: the coding agent *warned* about the risk every time. Night Shift surfaces that warning in
the postmortem. Nobody reads it at 5 PM; Night Shift reads it at 3 AM. #neatHack [screenshot]

## 3 — first live benchmark
Ran 6 staged incidents on live models (Haiku agent, Sonnet investigator), all traced in neatlogs.
Run 1: the investigator found an API-drift bug instantly (KeyError in the v2 adapter, exact commit +
prompt) — then rated itself 0.5 confident, so policy refused to act alone. Fixed calibration.
Run 2: [results]. Investigations cost ~$0.09 each. #neatHack [link to evidence/benchmark]

## 4 — it chose not to wake me
A release made the agent retry a flaky carrier API. Night Shift diagnosed it, priced it at $8 until
morning, and deferred it with the fix attached instead of paging me. Judgment > alerts. #neatHack

## 5 — demo
Night Shift demo (3 min): [video link]. Deploy a bad release → detected → traced to the prompt →
priced → rolled back → verified → one page on my phone. Repo + evidence: [link] #neatHack

"""Compare two benchmark runs (Night Shift before vs after a change) and snapshot the latest run
for the static web build.

    uv run python -m bench.compare run1-live run3-live
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import shutil
import sys

from ops.settings import REPO_DIR

ROOT = REPO_DIR / "evidence" / "benchmark"


def load(run: str) -> list[dict]:
    return json.loads((ROOT / run / "results.json").read_text())


def main(before: str, after: str) -> None:
    a, b = load(before), load(after)
    by_a = {r["incident"]: r for r in a}
    lines = [f"# Night Shift improved: `{before}` → `{after}`", "",
             "Same six staged incidents, same live models. Between the runs we changed Night Shift itself, "
             "based on what run 1 showed (see the build log):", "",
             "- investigator: explicit confidence calibration; a diagnosis without a confidence is rejected and re-submitted",
             "- low-impact incidents are deferred to the morning instead of paging someone",
             "- impact is priced from the conversations after the change, re-measured after the investigation",
             "- neatlogs trace read-back uses the full trace context (selective fields are disabled server-side)",
             "", "| # | Incident | Run | Diagnosis | Action | Outcome | Detect → contain | At risk | LLM cost |",
             "|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|"]
    for rb in b:
        ra = by_a.get(rb["incident"])
        for tag, r in (("before", ra), ("after", rb)):
            if not r:
                continue
            lines.append(
                f"| {r['incident']} | {r['name']} | {tag} | {'✅' if r['type_correct'] else '❌'} {r['diagnosed_type']} "
                f"(conf {r['confidence']}) | {'✅' if r['action_correct'] else '❌'} {r['action']} ({r['action_mode']}) "
                f"| {r['status']} | {r['seconds_detect_to_mitigate'] if r['seconds_detect_to_mitigate'] is not None else '—'}s "
                f"| ${r['projected_loss_if_waiting'] or 0:,.0f} | ${r['nightshift_cost_usd']} |")
    score = lambda rs: sum(1 for r in rs if r["type_correct"] and r["action_correct"])  # noqa: E731
    lines += ["", f"**Handled correctly: {score(a)}/{len(a)} → {score(b)}/{len(b)}**", "",
              "Harbor's own before/during/after numbers for each incident (the production agent improving once "
              f"Night Shift acts) are in [`{after}/SUMMARY.md`]({after}/SUMMARY.md)."]
    (REPO_DIR / "evidence" / "before-after.md").write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n")
    shutil.copy(ROOT / after / "results.json", REPO_DIR / "web" / "public" / "benchmark.json")
    snap = json.loads((REPO_DIR / "web" / "public" / "benchmark.json").read_text())
    (REPO_DIR / "web" / "public" / "benchmark.json").write_text(json.dumps({"run": after, "results": snap}))
    print("\n".join(lines))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main(*sys.argv[1:3])

# Night Shift

**The on-call engineer for your AI agents.** Built for neatHack 2026.

It stops the bleeding by itself. It only wakes you for decisions that can't be undone.

At 3 AM a "harmless" change to a customer-support agent starts paying refunds it shouldn't. Every
request still returns HTTP 200. Night Shift notices from the business signals, investigates like a
senior SRE (neatlogs traces, deploy log, release diff, the Entire checkpoint and the developer's
prompt behind the change), prices the damage with the cfo.ai model, takes the reversible containment
action its pre-approved policy allows, replays the failed conversations to prove the fix, and pages
you once: *handled — here's what it cost, a permanent fix is waiting for your approval.*

> Autonomous within a pre-approved policy. A human approves anything irreversible.
> Incidents in the benchmark are staged on purpose so they are reproducible.

## For judges: 60 seconds

| neatHack evidence | Where |
|---|---|
| The agent completes a substantial task | Night Shift runs the whole incident lifecycle: detect → investigate → price → decide → contain → verify → report. [`backend/nightshift/`](backend/nightshift) · [benchmark summary](evidence/benchmark/) |
| Agent improved (before/after with numbers) | Night Shift itself: [`evidence/before-after.md`](evidence/before-after.md) (run 1 → run 3). The production agent: before / during / after tables per incident in each run's `SUMMARY.md` |
| Recovers from failures | Every incident is a failure it recovers from; verification failure auto-undoes the action ([`runner.py`](backend/nightshift/runner.py), test `test_failed_verification_undoes_action`) |
| Used neatlogs | SDK traces for every conversation and investigation; read-back over the neatlogs MCP; a detection created by Night Shift. [`evidence/neatlogs.md`](evidence/neatlogs.md) |
| Used Entire | Every bad release was written by a separate Claude Code session and checkpointed; Night Shift resolves commit → checkpoint → prompt → the coding agent's warning, plus entire-graph change lists. [`evidence/entire.md`](evidence/entire.md) |
| Used cfo.ai | Incident pricing from the business model; the Night Shift business plan (pricing, costs, revenue, runway). [`business/`](business) |
| Built in public | [`posts/`](posts) |
| Code written during the hackathon | Commit history (first commit: plan only) |

## How it works

```
 customers ──► HARBOR support agent (Claude Haiku via LiteLLM) ──► tools ──► ledger
                    │ every call traced (neatlogs SDK)
                    ▼
 NIGHT SHIFT  1 WATCH       ledger vs policy, failed replies, tool errors, cost, escalations
              2 INVESTIGATE Claude Sonnet + tools: neatlogs MCP traces, deploy log, release diff,
                            Entire checkpoint → developer prompt, entire-graph change list
              3 PRICE       $/min at production volume × minutes until a human answers (cfo.ai model)
              4 DECIDE      policy/oncall-policy.yaml: reversible? confident? worth it?
              5 CONTAIN     roll back · fail over model · disable auto-refunds · cap steps
              6 VERIFY      replay the exact failed conversations; watch live traffic; auto-undo
              7 REPORT      page (ntfy) · postmortem · regression eval · fix proposal · neatlogs detection
```

Full spec: [`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md). Plan: [`docs/PLAN.md`](docs/PLAN.md). Spikes:
[`docs/SPIKES.md`](docs/SPIKES.md). Demo script: [`docs/DEMO_SCRIPT.md`](docs/DEMO_SCRIPT.md).

## Results

See [`evidence/benchmark/`](evidence/benchmark) — each run has `SUMMARY.md`, `results.json`, per-incident
postmortems written by Night Shift, and the regression evals it generated.

## Run it

```bash
cp .env.example .env            # LITELLM_API_KEY, NEATLOGS_API_KEY, optional NTFY_TOPIC
scripts/dev.sh                  # API on :8000 (live models) + console on :3000
scripts/dev.sh sim              # offline deterministic brain, no keys needed

cd backend && uv run pytest     # 16 tests
uv run python -m bench.benchmark --brain live   # the incident benchmark (~$1.5 of gateway credit)
```

Console: deploy a bad release (each one was written by a real Claude Code session), start a provider
outage or an attack wave, and watch Night Shift handle it. Turn Night Shift off to see what happens
without it.

## Repo map

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `backend/harbor/` | The production agent: tools, releases (r41 good; r42–r46 written by coding-agent sessions), grader, traffic |
| `backend/nightshift/` | Detector, investigator, provenance (git + Entire + entire-graph), impact, policy, actions, verifier, notifier, reporter, runner |
| `backend/api/` | FastAPI runtime + SSE for the console |
| `backend/bench/` | Incident benchmark and run comparison |
| `web/` | Next.js console and site |
| `policy/oncall-policy.yaml` | What Night Shift may do alone |
| `business/` | Unit economics (mirrors cfo.ai), business plan model, Ari prompts |
| `evidence/` | Benchmark runs, before/after, neatlogs and Entire evidence |

## Honest limitations

- Production traffic is simulated customers drawn from a scenario bank; tools act on a sandbox ledger.
- The provider outage is injected in our gateway client; prompt-injection traffic is generated.
- The `sim` brain exists for offline demos and is never used for evidence.
- The permanent fix is proposed, not applied: deploying code is a human decision by design.

from nightshift import provenance
from nightshift.neatlogs_mcp import NeatlogsMCP, NeatlogsMCPError
from ops.settings import REPO_DIR


def neatlogs_md(run: str) -> str:
    m = NeatlogsMCP()
    who = m.whoami()
    results = json.loads((REPO_DIR / "evidence" / "benchmark" / run / "results.json").read_text())
    lines = ["# neatlogs evidence", "",
             f"Project: **{who.get('project_name')}** (`{who.get('project_id')}`, tier {who.get('tier')}). "
             "Trace ids below can be searched in the neatlogs app.", "",
             "## How Night Shift uses neatlogs", "",
             "- **SDK tracing** (`ops/tracing.py`, `ops/llm.py`): every Harbor conversation is a WORKFLOW trace "
             "(`harbor-support`) with auto-instrumented LLM spans and a TOOL span per tool call; every Night Shift "
             "incident is a WORKFLOW trace (`nightshift`) containing the investigator's AGENT span, its TOOL spans and the "
             "verification replays.",
             "- **Read-back over MCP** (`nightshift/neatlogs_mcp.py`): the investigator calls `search_traces` and "
             "`get_trace_context` during an investigation and cites trace ids in its diagnosis and postmortem.",
             "- **Detections** (`nightshift/reporter.py`): after a prompt-injection incident Night Shift creates a regex "
             "detection for the attack signature so future traces are flagged.", ""]
    for wf in ("harbor-support", "nightshift"):
        try:
            res = m.search_traces("conversation" if wf == "harbor-support" else "incident", limit=1, workflow_name=wf)
            lines.append(f"- `{wf}` traces matching a sample query: {res.get('total')}")
        except NeatlogsMCPError as exc:
            lines.append(f"- `{wf}`: search failed ({exc})")
    try:
        det = m.list_detections()
        names = [d.get("display_name") or d.get("name") for d in (det.get("detections", det) if isinstance(det, dict) else det) or []
                 if isinstance(d, dict)]
        lines.append(f"- Active detections: {', '.join(n for n in names if n) or '—'}")
    except NeatlogsMCPError as exc:
        lines.append(f"- detections: {exc}")
    lines += ["", f"## Traces from benchmark run `{run}`", "",
              "| Incident | Night Shift investigation trace | Evidence traces cited | Before (baseline) | During | After |",
              "|---|---|---|---|---|---|"]
    for r in results:
        lines.append(f"| {r['incident']} {r['name']} | `{r['nightshift_trace_id']}` | "
                     + ", ".join(f"`{t}`" for t in r["evidence_trace_ids"][:3])
                     + f" | `{(r['before']['trace_ids'] or ['—'])[0]}` | `{(r['during']['trace_ids'] or ['—'])[0]}` "
                       f"| `{(r['after']['trace_ids'] or ['—'])[0]}` |")
    sample = next((r for r in results if r.get("evidence_trace_ids")), None)
    if sample:
        tid = sample["evidence_trace_ids"][0]
        try:
            ctx = m.get_trace_context(tid, max_chars_per_field=200)
            lines += ["", f"## One trace, read back through the MCP (`{tid}`)", "", "```json",
                      json.dumps({k: ctx.get(k) for k in ("trace_id", "workflow", "status", "llm_calls", "tool_calls",
                                                          "total_tokens", "latency_ms", "span_count")}, indent=2),
                      "```", "", "| span | type | status |", "|---|---|---|"]
            for s in (ctx.get("spans") or [])[:12]:
                lines.append(f"| {s.get('name')} | {s.get('type')} | {s.get('status')} |")
        except NeatlogsMCPError as exc:
            lines.append(f"\n(trace read-back failed: {exc})")
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"


def entire_md() -> str:
    lines = ["# Entire evidence", "",
             "Entire is enabled for Claude Code in this repo (`.entire/settings.json`, git-refs checkpoints, custom "
             "redaction rules). Two uses:", "",
             "1. **Development**: this repo's commits carry `Entire-Checkpoint:` trailers linking each change to the "
             "coding-agent session that produced it.",
             "2. **Runtime provenance**: every Harbor release after r41 was written by a *separate* Claude Code session "
             "(`claude -p` with a realistic developer request). When a release causes an incident, Night Shift follows "
             "release → commit → checkpoint → the developer's prompt and the coding agent's final note, plus the "
             "entire-graph semantic change list (`nightshift/provenance.py`).", "",
             "## Releases and the sessions behind them", "",
             "| Release | Commit | Checkpoint | Session | Agent / model | Developer prompt |", "|---|---|---|---|---|---|"]
    for rel in releases.list_releases():
        p = provenance.for_release(rel.id)
        prompt = (p.coding_prompts[0] if p.coding_prompts else "—").replace("|", "/").replace("\n", " ")[:160]
        lines.append(f"| {rel.id} {rel.title} | [`{(p.commit or '')[:8]}`]({p.entire_url}) | `{p.checkpoint_id}` | "
                     f"`{(p.session_id or '')[:8]}` | {p.agent} {p.model} | {prompt} |")
    lines += ["", "## What the coding agents warned (and nobody read)", ""]
    for rel in releases.list_releases():
        if rel.id == releases.BASELINE_RELEASE:
            continue
        p = provenance.for_release(rel.id)
        if p.coding_agent_note:
            lines += [f"### {rel.id} — {rel.title}", "", "> " + p.coding_agent_note.replace("\n", "\n> "), ""]
    lines += ["## entire-graph: what r43 changed", "", "```", provenance.for_release("r43").graph_changes or "—", "```", "",
              "## Checkpoints on this branch", "", "```"]
    out = subprocess.run(["entire", "checkpoint", "list"], cwd=REPO_DIR, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=60)
    lines += [out.stdout.strip()[:6000], "```"]
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"


if __name__ == "__main__":
    run = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "run3-live"
    (REPO_DIR / "evidence" / "neatlogs.md").write_text(neatlogs_md(run))
    (REPO_DIR / "evidence" / "entire.md").write_text(entire_md())
    print("wrote evidence/neatlogs.md and evidence/entire.md")

#!/bin/bash
# Rewrite checkpoint refs whose blobs contain key fragments, replacing them with REDACTED.
set -e
cd /home/user/neat-hacks
PAT='REDACTED[A-Za-z0-9_-]*|REDACTED[A-Za-z0-9_-]*'
for r in $(git for-each-ref --format='%(refname)' refs/entire); do
  dirty=0
  for line in $(git ls-tree -r $r | awk '{print $3"|"$4}'); do
    b=${line%%|*}; if git cat-file -p $b | grep -qE "$PAT"; then dirty=1; fi
  done
  [ $dirty = 1 ] || continue
  export GIT_INDEX_FILE=/tmp/claude-0/scrub.idx; rm -f $GIT_INDEX_FILE
  git read-tree $r
  for line in $(git ls-tree -r $r | awk '{print $1"|"$3"|"$4}'); do
    mode=${line%%|*}; rest=${line#*|}; b=${rest%%|*}; path=${rest#*|}
    if git cat-file -p $b | grep -qE "$PAT"; then
      nb=$(git cat-file -p $b | sed -E "s/$PAT/REDACTED/g" | git hash-object -w --stdin)
      git update-index --cacheinfo $mode,$nb,$path
    fi
  done
  t=$(git write-tree); unset GIT_INDEX_FILE
  msg=$(git log -1 --format=%B $r)
  c=$(GIT_AUTHOR_DATE="$(git log -1 --format=%aD $r)" git -c commit.gpgsign=false commit-tree $t -m "$msg")

  echo "scrubbed $r"
done
EOF

Night Shift is fully built and working, but **none of it is on GitHub yet**: your repo gives the Claude GitHub App read-only access, so every push and PR attempt failed with a 403. Everything is committed locally, split into 7 phase branches, and pushes in a minute once you grant write access.

**What I built**
- **Harbor:** a real customer-support agent on Claude Haiku (through your LiteLLM key) that handles refunds using tools. Every conversation is traced in neatlogs.
- **Bad releases:** 5 of them (r42–r46), each written by a separate Claude Code session from a realistic developer request, each with its own Entire checkpoint. Every one of those coding sessions warned about the risk, and the console shows that warning.
- **Night Shift:** detects the incident, investigates with Claude Sonnet, traces the deploy to its commit, Entire checkpoint and the developer's prompt (plus entire-graph's list of what changed), prices the damage in dollars, and acts only within a policy you approve ahead of time.
  - Its actions (rollback, model failover, switching off auto-refunds, capping steps) are all undoable.
  - It proves each fix by replaying the failed conversations, pages your phone through ntfy, and writes a postmortem and a regression test.
  - It created a real "Order-note prompt injection" detection in your neatlogs project.
- **UI (Next.js, styled after maritime.sh but not copied):** landing page, a live console (money-lost counter, live conversation feed, incident timeline, phone mock, buttons to ship bad releases or trigger an outage or attack), plus incidents, benchmark and business pages. I screenshot-checked it at desktop and mobile widths.

**Results on live models (6 deliberately staged incidents)**

| Incident | What Night Shift did | Seconds from detection to fix | Replays passing |
|---|---|---|---|
| Unchecked refunds | rolled back | 20.6 | 5/5 |
| Orders-API change broke lookups | rolled back | 20.8 | 5/5 |
| Flaky-API retry loop | deferred to morning (only ~$1 at risk, so no page) | — | — |
| Model provider outage | switched to backup model | 14.0 | 4/5 |
| Prompt-injection wave | rolled back | 16.1 | 5/5 |
| Ticket flood | rolled back | 15.6 | 4/4 |

- **Self-improvement:** the first run scored 4/6. Night Shift once rated its own confidence too low to act alone, and once paged a human at 3 AM for an $8 problem. I fixed both, and the same benchmark then scored 6/6. That before/after comparison is the evidence judges ask for that the agent improved.
- **Cost:** each investigation costs $0.05–0.15. Total gateway spend so far is $3.28 of $20.
- **Tests:** 16 tests pass, and the web build is clean.

**Two things you should know**
- **Key fragment in local checkpoints:** a scan found an 11-character fragment of your LiteLLM key inside Entire's stored session transcripts. The full keys were already redacted; the fragment came from my own leak-check commands. I widened the redaction rules and scrubbed the affected checkpoints, and a re-scan shows 0 matches. content.content:
37:A **one-of-each-type** rule permits two distinct git-backed backends in the same topology. Note, though, that the branch→refs migration deliberately does **not** run `git-branch` as a mirror of `git-refs`. Cross-format compatibility comes from read routing — every reader (CLI, entire.io, entire-api) reads refs first and falls back to the branch — not from dual-writing the same checkpoint into both backends (see [Migration and coexistence](#migration-and-coexistence)). Mirroring stays available as a general mechanism, primarily for non-git-backed targets (e.g. a filesystem store).
198:`checkpoint.Open` returns a `kindRoutingStore` (`checkpoint/routing_store.go`) that resolves id-keyed reads — and backfill writes — across **both** git backends by the checkpoint's ID kind, so a repo running git-refs and git-branch side by side (or mid-migration) handles either format without reconfiguring:
204:| **hex**, git-refs primary | refs first, then git-branch fallback | a hex checkpoint may still sit on the pre-migration v1 branch, or have been migrated into refs |
227:- **A first-time `entire enable` writes `git-refs` explicitly, with no prompt.** Both setup paths do it — the interactive flow and the non-interactive `--agent` flow — via `resolveFirstRunCheckpointBackend` / `firstRunCheckpointBackendDefault` (`setup.go`). There is deliberately **no setup question**: storage topology is not answerable at first-run, so the recommended backend is written silently and `git-branch` is reachable only by typing `--checkpoint-backend branch`. The one case that writes nothing is an active `ENTIRE_CHECKPOINTS_PRIMARY`, since the env fully replaces the settings block and persisting a default would only record diverging config.
256:This is why running `git-branch` as a *mirror* of git-refs is **not** part of the migration: it would dual-write every checkpoint into both backends to keep `v1` populated, but no reader needs that — read routing already covers both formats, and an old client not reading the new format is an accepted consequence rather than something to paper over. It is now a **silent** one: the `checkpoint_min_version` policy that used to turn it into an explicit "upgrade" nudge was removed with the checkpoint policy feature, and nothing replaced it. An old CLI in a refs-primary repo sees a partial history and is told nothing.
281:- **The "ULIDs never land on the branch" invariant is not yet enforced at write time.** A config flip or a missing `ENTIRE_CHECKPOINTS_PRIMARY` in an amending environment could, in principle, condense a ULID checkpoint onto the `v1` branch, which readers (routing ULIDs to refs only) would then fail to find. Because git-branch is *not* a mirror of git-refs (see [Migration and coexistence](#migration-and-coexistence)), a ULID reaching the git-branch write path is unambiguously a bug — so enforcing this is a straightforward reject at that write path, not a topology-role-aware check.

37:A **one-of-each-type** rule permits two distinct git-backed backends in the same topology. Note, though, that the branch→refs migration deliberately does **not** run `git-branch` as a mirror of `git-refs`. Cross-format compatibility comes from read routing — every reader (CLI, entire.io, entire-api) reads refs first and falls back to the branch — not from dual-writing the same checkpoint into both backends (see [Migration and coexistence](#migration-and-coexistence)). Mirroring stays available as a general mechanism, primarily for non-git-backed targets (e.g. a filesystem store).
198:`checkpoint.Open` returns a `kindRoutingStore` (`checkpoint/routing_store.go`) that resolves id-keyed reads — and backfill writes — across **both** git backends by the checkpoint's ID kind, so a repo running git-refs and git-branch side by side (or mid-migration) handles either format without reconfiguring:
204:| **hex**, git-refs primary | refs first, then git-branch fallback | a hex checkpoint may still sit on the pre-migration v1 branch, or have been migrated into refs |
227:- **A first-time `entire enable` writes `git-refs` explicitly, with no prompt.** Both setup paths do it — the interactive flow and the non-interactive `--agent` flow — via `resolveFirstRunCheckpointBackend` / `firstRunCheckpointBackendDefault` (`setup.go`). There is deliberately **no setup question**: storage topology is not answerable at first-run, so the recommended backend is written silently and `git-branch` is reachable only by typing `--checkpoint-backend branch`. The one case that writes nothing is an active `ENTIRE_CHECKPOINTS_PRIMARY`, since the env fully replaces the settings block and persisting a default would only record diverging config.
256:This is why running `git-branch` as a *mirror* of git-refs is **not** part of the migration: it would dual-write every checkpoint into both backends to keep `v1` populated, but no reader needs that — read routing already covers both formats, and an old client not reading the new format is an accepted consequence rather than something to paper over. It is now a **silent** one: the `checkpoint_min_version` policy that used to turn it into an explicit "upgrade" nudge was removed with the checkpoint policy feature, and nothing replaced it. An old CLI in a refs-primary repo sees a partial history and is told nothing.
281:- **The "ULIDs never land on the branch" invariant is not yet enforced at write time.** A config flip or a missing `ENTIRE_CHECKPOINTS_PRIMARY` in an amending environment could, in principle, condense a ULID checkpoint onto the `v1` branch, which readers (routing ULIDs to refs only) would then fail to find. Because git-branch is *not* a mirror of git-refs (see [Migration and coexistence](#migration-and-coexistence)), a ULID reaching the git-branch write path is unambiguously a bug — so enforcing this is a straightforward reject at that write path, not a topology-role-aware check.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# One-time: move Entire checkpoints from temporary `_entire/*` branches to `refs/entire/*`,
# where Entire and entire.io read them. (The build sandbox could only push branches.)
# Run from a clone of the repo with normal GitHub push access.
set -euo pipefail
git fetch origin '+refs/heads/_entire/*:refs/entire/*'
git push origin 'refs/entire/*:refs/entire/*'
for b in $(git ls-remote --heads origin '_entire/*' | awk '{print $2}'); do
  git push origin --delete "${b#refs/heads/}"
done
echo "Entire checkpoints restored to refs/entire/*"
EOF
chmod +x scripts/restore_entire_refs.sh

content.text:
That error suggests cfo.ai's sign-in doesn't support the device-code flow: its login has to go through cfo.ai's own page, which the device page skips. I'll switch to the standard browser login.

After you approve, your browser will try to open a `localhost` page that won't load. That's expected. Copy the full address from the address bar and paste it here. Setting it up:

"""cfo.ai MCP login with the browser (authorization code + PKCE), for machines without a local browser.

    uv run python scripts/cfo_oauth.py start            # prints a link; approve it in your browser
    uv run python scripts/cfo_oauth.py finish '<URL>'   # paste the localhost URL you were redirected to

The token is saved to <repo>/.cfo_token.json (gitignored).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import base64
import hashlib
import json
import secrets
import sys
import time
import urllib.parse
from pathlib import Path

import httpx

AUTH = "https://complete-cottage-73.authkit.app"
MCP = "https://api.cfo.ai/mcp"
REDIRECT = "http://localhost:8765/callback"
ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
STATE_FILE = ROOT / ".cfo_oauth_state.json"
TOKEN_FILE = ROOT / ".cfo_token.json"


def start() -> None:
    reg = httpx.post(f"{AUTH}/oauth2/register", json={
        "client_name": "Night Shift", "grant_types": ["authorization_code", "refresh_token"],
        "token_endpoint_auth_method": "none", "redirect_uris": [REDIRECT], "response_types": ["code"],
    }, timeout=20)
    reg.raise_for_status()
    client_id = reg.json()["client_id"]
    verifier = secrets.token_urlsafe(64)
    challenge = base64.urlsafe_b64encode(hashlib.sha256(verifier.encode()).digest()).rstrip(b"=").decode()
    state = secrets.token_urlsafe(16)
    STATE_FILE.write_text(json.dumps({"client_id": client_id, "verifier": verifier, "state": state}))
    STATE_FILE.chmod(0o600)
    q = urllib.parse.urlencode({
        "response_type": "code", "client_id": client_id, "redirect_uri": REDIRECT,
        "code_challenge": challenge, "code_challenge_method": "S256", "state": state,
        "scope": "openid profile email offline_access", "resource": MCP,
    })
    print(f"{AUTH}/oauth2/authorize?{q}")


def finish(url: str) -> None:
    st = json.loads(STATE_FILE.read_text())
    params = dict(urllib.parse.parse_qsl(urllib.parse.urlparse(url.strip()).query))
    if params.get("error"):
        sys.exit(f"authorization error: {params}")
    if params.get("state") != st["state"]:
        sys.exit("state mismatch — start again")
    r = httpx.post(f"{AUTH}/oauth2/token", data={
        "grant_type": "authorization_code", "code": params["code"], "redirect_uri": REDIRECT,
        "client_id": st["client_id"], "code_verifier": st["verifier"], "resource": MCP,
    }, timeout=20)
    body = r.json()
    if "access_token" not in body:
        sys.exit(f"token exchange failed: {body}")
    body["client_id"] = st["client_id"]
    body["obtained_at"] = time.time()
    TOKEN_FILE.write_text(json.dumps(body))
    TOKEN_FILE.chmod(0o600)
    STATE_FILE.unlink(missing_ok=True)
    print("logged in; token saved")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    if sys.argv[1:2] == ["start"]:
        start()
    elif sys.argv[1:2] == ["finish"]:
        finish(sys.argv[2])
    else:
        sys.exit(__doc__)
EOF

"""Refresh the saved cfo.ai token and write an MCP config file for Claude Code.

    uv run python scripts/cfo_token.py /path/to/mcp.json
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

import httpx

TOKEN_FILE = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / ".cfo_token.json"


def refresh() -> dict:
    d = json.loads(TOKEN_FILE.read_text())
    r = httpx.post("https://complete-cottage-73.authkit.app/oauth2/token", data={
        "grant_type": "refresh_token", "refresh_token": d["refresh_token"], "client_id": d["client_id"]}, timeout=20)
    b = r.json()
    if "access_token" not in b:
        sys.exit(f"refresh failed: {b}")
    b["client_id"] = d["client_id"]
    b["obtained_at"] = time.time()
    b.setdefault("refresh_token", d["refresh_token"])
    TOKEN_FILE.write_text(json.dumps(b))
    return b


if __name__ == "__main__":
    tok = refresh()
    out = Path(sys.argv[1])
    out.write_text(json.dumps({"mcpServers": {"cfoai": {"type": "http", "url": "https://api.cfo.ai/mcp",
                                                         "headers": {"Authorization": f"Bearer {tok['access_token']}"}}}}))
    out.chmod(0o600)
    print("refreshed; expires_in", tok.get("expires_in"))
EOF

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /root/.claude/skills/synced/274ae7c1-4263-4cf1-a02f-b3c3a4889b77_79a78098-bb96-4c53-b522-2415796b2631/built-in-browser

# Built-in browser

The built-in browser is a real browser pane inside the Claude desktop app, separate from the person's Chrome. Its tools are named `mcp__Claude_Browser__*` when the session itself runs inside the desktop app, and `mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__*` when the session runs in the cloud (started from the web, a phone, or the desktop app) and is linked to the person's computer. The names after the prefix are the same either way, Claude uses whichever prefix is actually present, and this skill refers to the tools by the part after the prefix.

If the only built-in browser tool present is `enable__mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser`, Claude calls it first: it turns the built-in browser on for this conversation, and the `mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__*` tools appear once it has run.

## What the person can see

The browser pane shares the desktop app's side panel with artifacts, documents, and file previews, and the panel shows one of them at a time. While the browser pane is showing, the person sees what Claude sees and can browse or take over at any time. While something else is open in the panel, or the panel is closed, the built-in browser keeps working but the person cannot see it.

Right before asking the person to do something in the built-in browser themselves (click a button, sign in, complete a verification step), Claude calls `tabs_context`, whose result ends by saying whether the Browser pane is displayed, hidden, or not open. If the pane is not open, Claude opens the page first and checks again. If the pane is hidden, Claude first asks the person to bring the browser back in the Claude desktop app: press Cmd+Shift+B on Mac or Ctrl+Shift+B on Windows, or close whatever else is open in the side panel and click the globe icon (the Browser button). Claude then says what to do in the browser. Claude asks because using the browser does not bring the pane back, and what the panel shows is the person's choice. Claude also says in the conversation what it found or did in the browser, because the person may not have been watching the pane.

## Sign-ins persist, and they are the person's

The built-in browser keeps its own persistent profile, shared across the desktop app's sessions. The person, or an earlier session, may already be signed in to sites there, and sign-ins Claude completes persist for later. Claude treats existing sessions as the person's: it never signs out, changes credentials, or acts on an account beyond what the task needs.

## Tabs

The built-in browser has tabs. `preview_start` with a `url` opens an additional tab at that URL in one call and returns a `tabId`, leaving existing tabs untouched, so Claude prefers it over `tabs_create` followed by `navigate` when the destination is already known. `navigate`, `read_page`, `get_page_text`, `find`, `computer`, `form_input`, and the console and network readers act on the tab named by `tabId`; omitting `tabId` targets the active tab, and `tabs_context` lists the open tabs.

## Loading via ToolSearch

Claude loads the built-in browser tools in bulk, not one-by-one: if they are in the deferred list, Claude loads them all in a single ToolSearch call whose query is their full name prefix, for example `{ query: "mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__", max_results: 64 }`.

## Reading pages

Claude prefers `get_page_text` and `read_page` over screenshots for reading, because they return the page's actual text and structure rather than pixels of the visible viewport. `computer` with action "screenshot" is for when the visual layout is the point or the person asks to see the page.

## Site approvals, blocked sites, and request_access

Depending on the person's approval settings, the person may be asked to approve a site before Claude acts on it, and some sites are blocked outright. Claude waits for a pending approval rather than working around it. If a page is refused or an approval is declined, Claude tells the person and moves on rather than retrying.

When the tools carry the `mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__` prefix, approvals can be answered from any of the person's devices and may take a moment to arrive, and the session may also have a `request_access` tool. If a browser tool answers that the site is not allowed yet and `request_access` is present, Claude calls it with that site's URL and scope "once" (or "site" when the task will keep using that site), waits for the person's answer, and then retries the original tool. Without `request_access`, a refused site is handled as above: Claude tells the person and moves on.

## What the built-in browser cannot open

The built-in browser cannot open `file://` URLs or `localhost` servers that Claude starts itself, because those run where Claude's shell runs, which is not where the browser pane runs. To show the person HTML that Claude generated, Claude uses an artifact instead.

## When the built-in browser cannot be reached

When the tools carry the `mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__` prefix, the pane runs in the Claude desktop app on the person's computer while Claude runs elsewhere, so it is reachable only while that app is open and online. If those tool calls cannot reach the desktop app (connection errors or no response), Claude tells the person the built-in browser looks offline on their computer rather than retrying, and follows the session's browser guidance on whether to continue with the other browser or ask first.

message.content: I wen through the project but it does not seem like a product, seems like a dummy site I don't know what, how to productize it?, what's msissing?

content.text:
I agree, and I can name why. Night Shift's engine is real (live models, real traces, real checkpoints), but everything around it is a demo harness, so the site reads like one.

## Why it feels like a dummy site

1. **It only watches its own toy agent.** Harbor, the fake store and the simulated customers are the only thing it can monitor. A visitor can't point it at *their* agent, and that's the single biggest gap.
2. **The main screen is a demo control panel.** Buttons like "Ship a release", "Provider outage" and "Prompt-injection wave" sit next to the real data. Products don't have a "break production" button; test harnesses do.
3. **The actions only work on our own sandbox.** "Roll back" flips a value inside our own SQLite. Real teams roll back through GitHub, their deploy platform, feature flags or the model router.
4. **There's no product shell.** No sign-up or workspace, no "connect" steps, no list of your agents, no policy editor (the policy is a YAML file), no notification settings, no incident inbox with approvals.
5. **The detector only works for Harbor.** It reads Harbor's refund ledger. A real product has to work from signals any traced agent has: errors, tool failures, cost, latency and neatlogs detections.

## What turns it into a product

**Positioning:** "Connect your neatlogs project and your repo. Night Shift watches your agent and handles incidents within the policy you set."

| Piece | What it adds | Est. time |
|---|---|---|
| **Onboarding wizard** (`/app/connect`) | Paste a neatlogs project key (we check it live), connect the GitHub repo with Entire, pick a policy template, add Slack or ntfy for paging. Creates a workspace. | ~3h |
| **Generic detection from neatlogs** | Watches any agent's traces: error rate, tool errors, cost and latency spikes, neatlogs detections firing. The Harbor ledger becomes an optional "business signal" plug-in. | ~3h |
| **Control SDK (`pip install nightshift`)** | Three calls in the customer's agent: `ns.release()`, `ns.flag("auto_refunds")`, `ns.model()`. Night Shift's rollback, failover and kill-switch then work on *any* agent. Harbor becomes the reference example. | ~2h |
| **Real fix PRs** | The "permanent fix" becomes a real GitHub PR (revert of the bad commit plus the regression test), opened for human approval. This is the irreversible step done properly. | ~1.5h |
| **App shell** | `/app` with Incidents inbox (approve/reject), Agents, Policy editor (form over the YAML), Integrations, Settings. The marketing site stays separate. | ~4h |
| **Demo becomes a sandbox** | Move the chaos buttons to `/sandbox` ("Try Night Shift on a sample agent"). Harbor is clearly labelled as the sample customer. | ~1h |

That's about 14–15 hours; the deadline is tonight, Oct 12, 7–11:55 PM IST. It fits, but it competes with the demo video and posts, which together are 35% of the score.

My recommendation: do the onboarding wizard, generic neatlogs detection, the control SDK and the sandbox split first (about 9 hours). Those four make it clearly a product someone else could use. Real fix PRs and the full app shell come after, if time allows.

## What I need from you

1. **Scope:** the full list, or the four-piece core (onboarding, generic detection, SDK, sandbox split)?
2. **Proof it works on another agent:** should the demo include a second, different agent connected through the onboarding flow (for example a small research agent)? Judges then see it isn't hard-wired to Harbor. I recommend yes; it's about 1.5 hours.
3. **Accounts:** a simple single-user workspace (no login), or real sign-in? I recommend single-user for the hackathon, with sign-in shown as next steps.
4. **Slack:** do you have a Slack workspace for paging? If not, I'll keep ntfy plus a generic webhook.

Tell me your picks and I'll start. The cfo.ai session is still running in the background either way.

+"""Auth primitives: user session tokens (minted by the web app), agent SDK tokens, internal calls,
+and encryption of stored secrets (neatlogs keys, GitHub and Slack tokens).
+
+- User tokens are HS256 JWTs signed with NS_AUTH_SECRET, which the web app shares. The web app mints
+  one after GitHub sign-in; the browser sends it as a bearer token (or `?token=` for SSE).
+- Agent tokens (`nsa_…`) are random; only their SHA-256 is stored.
+- Internal calls (web server → API, e.g. upserting a user after sign-in) carry NS_INTERNAL_SECRET.
+- Secrets at rest are Fernet-encrypted with NS_ENCRYPTION_KEY (derived from NS_AUTH_SECRET if unset).
+
+When NS_AUTH_SECRET is unset the API runs in local dev mode with a single "dev" user.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import base64
+import hashlib
+import hmac
+import os
+import secrets
+import time
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from typing import Any
+
+import jwt
+from cryptography.fernet import Fernet, InvalidToken
+
+ALGO = "HS256"
+
+
+def _env(name: str) -> str:
+    return os.environ.get(name, "").strip()
+
+
+def auth_secret() -> str:
+    return _env("NS_AUTH_SECRET")
+
+
+def dev_mode() -> bool:
+    return not auth_secret()
+
+
+@dataclass
+class Principal:
+    user_id: str
+    login: str
+    name: str | None = None
+    avatar_url: str | None = None
+
+
+DEV_PRINCIPAL = Principal(user_id="dev", login="dev", name="Local developer")
+
+
+def mint_user_token(p: Principal, ttl_s: int = 3600) -> str:
+    now = int(time.time())
+    return jwt.encode({"sub": p.user_id, "login": p.login, "name": p.name, "avatar": p.avatar_url,
+                       "iat": now, "exp": now + ttl_s, "aud": "nightshift-api"}, auth_secret(), algorithm=ALGO)
+
+
+def verify_user_token(token: str) -> Principal | None:
+    if dev_mode():
+        return DEV_PRINCIPAL
+    try:
+        claims = jwt.decode(token, auth_secret(), algorithms=[ALGO], audience="nightshift-api")
+    except jwt.PyJWTError:
+        return None
+    return Principal(user_id=str(claims["sub"]), login=claims.get("login") or "", name=claims.get("name"),
+                     avatar_url=claims.get("avatar"))
+
+
+def verify_internal(header_value: str | None) -> bool:
+    expected = _env("NS_INTERNAL_SECRET")
+    if not expected:
+        return dev_mode()
+    return bool(header_value) and hmac.compare_digest(header_value, expected)
+
+
+# -- agent tokens --------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+def new_agent_token() -> tuple[str, str, str]:
+    """Returns (token, sha256, display prefix)."""
+    token = "nsa_" + secrets.token_urlsafe(32)
+    return token, hash_token(token), token[:10]
+
+
+def hash_token(token: str) -> str:
+    return hashlib.sha256(token.encode()).hexdigest()
+
+
+# -- secrets at rest ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+def _fernet() -> Fernet:
+    key = _env("NS_ENCRYPTION_KEY")
+    if not key:
+        seed = auth_secret() or "nightshift-local-dev-only"
+        key = base64.urlsafe_b64encode(hashlib.sha256(("enc:" + seed).encode()).digest()).decode()
+    return Fernet(key.encode())
+
+
+def encrypt(value: str | None) -> str | None:
+    if not value:
+        return None
+    return _fernet().encrypt(value.encode()).decode()
+
+
+def decrypt(value: str | None) -> str | None:
+    if not value:
+        return None
+    try:
+        return _fernet().decrypt(value.encode()).decode()
+    except InvalidToken:
+        return None
+
+
+def mask(value: str | None, keep: int = 4) -> str | None:
+    if not value:
+        return None
+    return value[:keep] + "…" + value[-keep:] if len(value) > keep * 2 else "…"
+
+
+def sign_state(payload: dict[str, Any], ttl_s: int = 900) -> str:
+    """Signed, expiring state for OAuth round-trips (Slack install)."""
+    now = int(time.time())
+    return jwt.encode({**payload, "exp": now + ttl_s, "aud": "nightshift-state"},
+                      auth_secret() or "nightshift-local-dev-only", algorithm=ALGO)
+
+
+def verify_state(state: str) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
+    try:
+        return jwt.decode(state, auth_secret() or "nightshift-local-dev-only", algorithms=[ALGO],
+                          audience="nightshift-state")
+    except jwt.PyJWTError:
+        return None
