cat > getting-started.md <<'EOF'
# Getting started with Lumen

Lumen is a product analytics platform. You send events from your app, and Lumen turns them into funnels, retention charts and dashboards.

## Create a project

Every workspace starts with one project. Create more projects from **Settings → Projects**. Each project has its own write key, and events never mix between projects.

## Install the snippet

Install the JavaScript SDK with `npm install @lumen/browser` and call `lumen.init("<write key>")` once on page load. Server-side SDKs exist for Node, Python and Go.

## Your first event

Call `lumen.track("Signed Up", { plan: "pro" })`. Events show up in the Live view within 10 seconds.
EOF
cat > billing.md <<'EOF'
# Billing and plans

Lumen has three plans: Free, Growth and Enterprise.

## Plan limits

The Free plan includes 1 million events per month and 1 year of data retention. Growth costs $49 per month per 5 million events and keeps data for 3 years. Enterprise is priced annually and keeps data for 7 years.

## Overages

When a Growth workspace goes over its event allowance, Lumen keeps ingesting and bills overage at $8 per additional million events. Free workspaces are paused at the limit instead; ingestion resumes on the first day of the next month.

## Refunds

Annual plans can be refunded pro rata within 30 days of the renewal date. Monthly plans are not refunded, but you can cancel at any time and keep access until the end of the billing period.

## Invoices

Invoices are emailed to the billing contact on the 1st of each month. Download past invoices from **Settings → Billing → Invoices**.
EOF
cat > sso.md <<'EOF'
# Single sign-on (SSO)

SSO is available on the Enterprise plan.

## Supported providers

Lumen supports SAML 2.0 with Okta, Azure AD (Entra ID), Google Workspace and OneLogin. OIDC is in beta.

## Enforce SSO

After the SAML connection passes a test login, an admin can turn on **Enforce SSO**. When SSO is enforced, password logins are disabled for every member except the workspace owner, who keeps a break-glass password.

## SCIM provisioning

SCIM provisioning creates and removes members automatically. Deprovisioned members lose access within 5 minutes.
EOF
cat > data-export.md <<'EOF'
# Exporting data

## CSV export

Any chart can be exported as CSV from the chart menu. CSV exports are capped at 50,000 rows.

## Warehouse sync

Growth and Enterprise workspaces can sync raw events to Snowflake, BigQuery or Redshift. Syncs run every 6 hours on Growth and every hour on Enterprise.

## Raw export API

The Export API returns raw events as gzipped NDJSON for a date range. Requests are limited to 31 days per call and 60 calls per hour.
EOF
cat > data-deletion.md <<'EOF'
# Deleting data

## Delete a user (GDPR)

Submit a deletion request with the user's distinct ID from **Privacy → Deletion requests** or the Privacy API. Lumen deletes the user's events from all projects within 30 days and sends a confirmation email when done.

## Delete events by name

Admins can hide an event name immediately. Permanently deleting all events with a given name is irreversible and takes up to 7 days.

## Delete a project

Deleting a project removes all of its data after a 14-day grace period, during which the owner can restore it.
EOF
cat > api-limits.md <<'EOF'
# API rate limits

## Ingestion

The ingestion endpoint accepts up to 1,000 events per request and 20,000 requests per minute per project. Requests above the limit get HTTP 429 with a `Retry-After` header.

## Query API

The Query API allows 120 queries per minute per workspace. Long-running queries time out after 60 seconds.

## Keys

Write keys can only send events. Read access needs a service account secret, created under **Settings → Service accounts**.
EOF
cat > funnels.md <<'EOF'
# Funnels

A funnel measures how many users complete a sequence of steps.

## Conversion window

By default a user must finish all steps within 7 days. You can set the conversion window anywhere from 1 minute to 90 days.

## Step limit

Funnels support up to 20 steps. Each step can filter on event properties.

## Holding constant

Hold a property constant (for example `device`) to only count users whose property value stays the same across every step.
EOF
cat > integrations.md <<'EOF'
# Integrations

## Slack

The Slack integration posts a chart or dashboard to a channel on a schedule, daily or weekly. Alerts can also be sent to Slack when a metric moves more than a threshold you set.

## Segment

Lumen can be added as a Segment destination. Events, identifies and page calls are mapped automatically.

## Webhooks

Cohort webhooks call your URL when a user enters or leaves a cohort. Webhooks retry for 24 hours with exponential backoff.
EOF
ls

+"""Scout: the docs Q&A assistant for Lumen, a (fictional) product analytics SaaS.

+outcomes, and runs verification replays when Night Shift asks.
+
+    python scout.py ask "How many steps can a funnel have?"

+    python scout.py deploy s2               # report a deploy (commit = last change to the release)
+    python scout.py eval --release s2       # offline eval over the question bank

+    s = sub.add_parser("serve")

cat > README.md <<'EOF'
# Scout

Scout is the docs assistant for Lumen, a fictional product analytics SaaS. It is the second agent
Night Shift watches, and it is wired the way a customer's agent would be:

- **neatlogs** traces every answer (workflow `scout-answers`, root span `scout_answer`, one span per tool call)
- the **Night Shift SDK** gives it its live release, model, step cap and kill switches, takes its deploy
  reports and graded outcomes, and runs verification replays
- nothing in Scout imports Night Shift's code

```bash
export NIGHTSHIFT_API_URL=https://<api>   NIGHTSHIFT_AGENT_TOKEN=nsa_...
uv run --project ../../backend python scout.py eval              # offline eval over questions.yaml
uv run --project ../../backend python scout.py deploy s1         # report a deploy
uv run --project ../../backend python scout.py serve --rate 6    # traffic + replay worker
```

Releases live in `releases/`. A release picks the model, retriever, `top_k`, step budget and prompt;
the code for every retriever ships together, so rolling back is a control-plane change.
EOF
cd /home/user/neat-hacks && git checkout -b nightshift/p9-scout && git add agents/scout && git commit -qm "Add Scout, a docs Q&A agent wired to Night Shift only through the SDK and neatlogs" && git log --oneline -1
